survivors.claim: D14 promise that a declared reconcile path is not exempt (declared-and-mutated is a contradiction the refusal names) is not delivered. Mafter is read at spec/scripts/replay.js:929 BEFORE the declared-path staging loop at :948, so a hook that rewrites a mutated file in the worktree only (the ordinary hook shape; this repo own hook stages nothing by hand) leaves the staged blob id untouched at Mafter time; the D2 staging step then stages the declared path carrying the hook bytes, the commit carries the hook rewrite of the defect, and the D3 exclusion removes the mutated file from the canonical patch entirely. Exit 0, HEAD moved, patch-out empty.
survivors.impact: When the reconcile hook rewrites a file the mutation also touches, the harness commits the hook version of the planted defect instead of refusing, and the patch every later phase scores against no longer contains the mutation at all, so the run measures a defect that was never planted and can never be caught.

A declared reconcile path is not exempt: a path that is both declared and mutated is a contradiction the refusal names. Contract step 9 orders Mafter -> exit 4 BEFORE the per-path add --

loop for (paths ∩ Dafter), which is the order the code implements at :929 vs :948: the promise and the step order contradict each other for a worktree-only rewrite, and the code follows the order. Discriminating control (pinned by the existing test: rewrites the mutation own file and re-stages it): the same hook with an explicit add lib/x.js appended IS refused with exit 4, i.e. the check only sees bytes the hook itself staged.

survivors.claim: D14 is index-keyed only, so a hook that rewrites a mutated file in the worktree without staging it passes every check (D14: staged blob unchanged; D2/D13: the path is already in D0 via the --cached list), commits the pristine mutation, and leaves the worktree dirty with the hook bytes. Phase 1 step 6 then runs review-legs with --root {dir}: the legs execute against the hook-altered worktree while the blind reviewer and --score read the committed mutation.
survivors.impact: The deterministic legs can test a version of the defect the hook rewrote while the reviewer judges the version that was committed, so a leg verdict and a reviewer verdict in the same run are about two different trees and the attribution ladder compares two different things.
survivors.evidence: Executed against the real entrypoint. Same fixture shape at base 22a1572, config {replay:{afterApply:{command:"printf x > derived.json; printf hookwrote > lib/x.js",paths:["derived.json"]}}}. --apply -> applied ..., exit=0. show HEAD:lib/x.js -> a/B/c (mutation committed intact). status --porcelain in S2/wt -> " M lib/x.js"; cat S2/wt/lib/x.js -> hookwrote. out.patch +++ headers -> +++ b/lib/x.js only (D3 exclusion of derived.json correct). replay.md:130-131: step 6 runs review-legs --root {dir} on that dirty worktree with no intervening checkout -- . D14 rationale says the check answers did-the-hook-alter-the-defect keyed on bytes, but the Decision text pins staged blob id, so this is a gap in the ruling reach rather than a deviation from its letter; medium because it is reachable on the doctrine path with any hook that touches a mutated file without staging (this repo size-ratchet hook does not).

survivors.claim: stagedBlobIds passes the mutated file names to ls-files -s -- as pathspecs, which are interpreted with glob semantics; a mutated path containing *, ? or [ is looked up as a pattern rather than a literal, so its own entry can be absent from both M0 and Mafter (undefined === undefined) and D14 is silently blind to it. :(literal) magic or --literal-pathspecs would close it.
survivors.impact: A mutated file whose name contains a shell-glob character would be exempt from the byte-freeze check without any error; unlikely in this repo, so advisory only.
survivors.evidence: Not executed (advisory). Read of :819 [-c core.quotePath=off ls-files -s -- ...files] with no literal-pathspec magic; pathspec docs treat *, ?, [ as wildcards by default.
